clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-666 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8481-exemption-ernest-g-dodge-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed July 12, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts Ernest G. Dodge from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, July 31, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending July 31, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of July 31, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when July 31, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses.
